articles.title: World Series 2026: Jackson Chourio ties Babe Ruth for most hits in first 4 games of a Fall Classic
articles.summary: Chourio recorded his ninth and 10th hits of this series in Milwaukee's Game 4 loss.
articles.body:
With the Milwaukee Brewers holding a 3-2 lead in the top of the 12th inning of Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday, Jackson Chourio came to the plate with a chance to put his name next to a legend's.

Chourio hit a two-out double off of Tampa Bay Rays reliever Ian Seymour. With that, he secured his 10th hit of the World Series, which tied Babe Ruth for the most by a player in the first four games of a Fall Classic.

Ruth's record had stood as his own since 1928. He secured his tally across a 4-0 New York Yankees sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals.

Chourio's hit continued a remarkable run for the 22-year-old slugger, who has been a threat in Milwaukee's lineup for the entirety of his three-season MLB career. He entered Game 4 slashing .286/.308/.429 this postseason with 2 home runs, 9 RBI and 3 stolen bases. He finished Tuesday's game 2-for-6 at the plate.

His 10th-inning hit was his 16th this postseason and his 31st through three postseasons. That moved him past Atlanta Braves Hall of Famer Andruw Jones for the most postseason hits by a player before turning 23. Chourio reached his tally in 21 fewer games than Jones.

Milwaukee took a 3-2 lead in the top of the 12th via a Cooper Pratt solo home run. But the Rays tied the game and loaded the bases with no outs in the bottom of the 12th.

Then Ben Williamson delivered a walk-off RBI single to secure a 4-3 Tampa Bay victory to fend off a sweep and cut Milwaukee's series lead to 3-1.

Game 5 is scheduled for 8 p.m. ET Wednesday in St. Petersburg.

articles.title: Rays' Nick Martinez Says Team is 'Capable' of Historic World Series Comeback After Walk-Off G4 Win
articles.summary: After keeping their season alive with a dramatic 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in 12 innings in Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday night, the Tampa Bay Rays got the glimmer of hope they need to believe a historic comeback is possible.
articles.body:
After keeping their season alive with a dramatic 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers in 12 innings in Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday night, the Tampa Bay Rays got the glimmer of hope they need to believe a historic comeback is possible.

Rays pitcher Nick Martinez told reporters after the win they are "capable" of becoming the first team in World Series history to overcome a 3-0 series deficit.

"Sometimes you just got to see one through," said Martinez, who pitched two scoreless innings in relief. "We can win four in a row. This team is capable of doing that."

The Brewers, who have been the comeback kids throughout this postseason, got to experience it from the other side when Tampa scored twice in the bottom of the 12th to get the win after Cooper Pratt put the NL champs up 3-2 in the top of the frame.

Milwaukee's loss snapped its eight-game playoff winning streak that was tied for the longest by any team in MLB history.

The most famous eight-game postseason win streak was the 2004 Boston Red Sox, who are still the only team to overcome a 3-0 deficit in a best-of-seven series in MLB history. They won four straight against the New York Yankees in the ALCS, then swept the St. Louis Cardinals in the World Series.

Tampa only has to win four straight games to capture its first championship. It would be a Herculean task if the Rays pull it off, but the first hurdle has been cleared.

The Brewers did have two losing streaks of at least four games in the regular season, though both of them came back in April.

Milwaukee will send Jacob Misiorowski to the mound in Game 5 on Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET looking to clinch its first World Series title in franchise history.

The Rays have not yet announced their starting pitcher. Martinez, who started Game 1, would have been in line to take the mound if he had not been used on Tuesday.

articles.title: Brewers' Christian Yelich Sounds Off on World Series G4 Loss, 'Not Supposed to Be Easy'
articles.summary: Outfielder and team captain Christian Yelich summed things up following the Milwaukee Brewers' heartbreaking, 4-3 loss in extra innings to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Outfielder and team captain Christian Yelich summed things up following the Milwaukee Brewers' heartbreaking, 4-3 loss in extra innings to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday.

Speaking to reporters after the Brewers allowed a golden opportunity to close out the series to slip through their fingers, Yelich said, "This stuff is not supposed to be easy. It's supposed to test you."

Trailing by scores of 1-0 and 2-1, the Brewers twice battled back to tie things up in Game 4 thanks to an RBI double by Cooper Pratt and solo home run by David Hamilton.

That allowed Milwaukee to force extra innings, and after the teams failed to score in the 10th and 11th innings, Pratt smacked a solo homer in the top of the 12th to put the Brewers ahead 3-2.

Milwaukee entered the bottom of the 12th needing three outs to win the first World Series in franchise history, but things went awry from there.

After Junior Caminero began the inning by reaching first base on a throwing error by Joey Ortiz, Shane Drohan entered the game and allowed four consecutive singles.

An RBI single by Jonny DeLuca tied it, and a walk-off RBI single by Ben Williamson won it, thus giving the Rays new life.

The Brewers still have a huge advantage, up 3-2 with likely National League Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski set to take the mound in Game 5 on Wednesday, but it is fair to wonder if losing Game 4 in such dramatic fashion could potentially mess with the Brew Crew's psyche.

articles.title: Fans debate Brewers decision to keep Jacob Misiorowski in dugout with chance to win first ever World Series
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers were three outs from a World Series sweep before Pat Murphy's decision to hold Jacob Misiorowski sparked fierce debate.
articles.body: It is hardly a new phenomenon to see starting pitchers - elite ones at that - get the final outs of the World Series, but the Milwaukee Brewers passed on that opportunity. Up 3-2 heading into the bottom of the 12th, the Brewers were three outs away from a sweep to win their first Fall Classic. Having used up plenty of relievers, manager Pat Murphy decided to keep impending Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski in the dugout and go with Shane Drohan. But Drohan, who got bitten by his defense, did not record an out, and a Game 5 will be played Wednesday night. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE After the game, Murphy said Misiorowski, who was always slated to, and will, start Game 5, was not an option. "You can't blow that type of situation on a one-run lead on the road," Murphy said. "If we were in the 13th inning and had a three-run lead, that might be a little bit different, and I probably still wouldn't have." The move was highly debated on social media in the early morning hours after the game. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I'm not crazy for thinking that the Brewers should have put in Misiorowski to start the inning, right? You need 3 outs, go use your best arm to get them," one X user said. "Not sure it gets as utter woke nonsense as saving the best pitcher in the world for a hypothetical game 5 where you’d still be up 3-1," said another. "Wouldn’t have needed a game 5 , congrats on out thinking yourself," added one more. And, of course, there's the contrary. YANKEES LEGEND SAYS HE DOES NOT 'FEEL WELCOME' BY TEAM DESPITE LEGENDARY CAREER "They had 3-0 game lead. No reason to throw Misiorowski in this game," one opposer said. "What if he had and Tampa still won. He would have lost him for at least game 5," a Rays fan wrote. Misiorowski pitched to an MLB-leading 1.80 ERA this season, and his 252 strikeouts and 13.0 K/9 were also league bests . He has not found similar success in October, but he's still fared quite nicely (2.70 ERA, 14 strikeouts in 13.1 innings spanning three starts). Had Misiorowski blown the save (an unlikely scenario), who knows who would pitch Game 5, but it's hard to imagine that he would not be available in a necessary Game 6 at home. Murphy went with seven relievers after starter Dustin May tossed just three innings. Trevor Megill was used for one batter in the eighth inning, and Aaron Ashby, who has now allowed a run in 18.0 innings, started the ninth and was taken out after recording one out in the 11th. First pitch is shortly after 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Yankees legend Jorge Posada says he doesn't 'feel welcome' around the team anymore
articles.summary: Jorge Posada spent all 17 of his MLB seasons with the Yankees.
articles.body:
Throughout the New York Yankees' late-'90s dynasty, few players epitomized the team better than Jorge Posada. His rise to prominence coincided with the Yankees' three-peat during the decade. From there, he remained a mainstay in the lineup over his 17-year MLB career.

Now, he no longer feels welcome around the team. Posada revealed that information during an appearance on the New York Post's baseball podcast.

When asked whether he would be a good candidate to help the team's coaching staff, Posada said, "I could, but I don't think they want me there to tell you the truth."

When asked why he believed that was the case, Posada followed up:

"I don't feel welcome when I go there. Even in spring training, I don't feel like … I don't feel welcome. I don't feel like they want me there, so I don't go."

Posada said he wasn't sure what caused his relationship with the team to change and expressed a desire to move forward. He added, however, that the final year of his career was difficult, and it's tough to relive those feelings when he returns to the team.

After 14 fantastic years as a mainstay with the team, Posada saw his numbers dip in his final year with the Yankees. Relegated to the team's designated hitter role, Posada hit just .235/.315/.398 in his final year. He was 40.

A few months later, he retired. Despite the Yankees not showing interest in bringing him back for another year, Posada retired as a member of the franchise and spoke highly of the Yankees during his retirement announcement.

While the Yankees have turned in some strong seasons since Posada's retirement, making the playoffs in 10 of 14 tries, the team hasn't won a World Series during that stretch. Despite a sense that things have stalled out under manager Aaron Boone, the team announced in October that he would be back as its manager for another season.

With Boone back, there's a belief the Yankees could benefit from some new blood elsewhere in the organization. Posada could provide that, and his word could carry some weight in the clubhouse considering his history with the organization.

For now, that type of role doesn't appear in the cards for Posada, at least not until he feels more welcome around his former team.

articles.title: New Mets Rumors on Teruaki Sato Reveal David Stearns' Scouting Trip After MLB Season
articles.summary: With Teruaki Sato set to be arguably the most sought-after position player in free agency, the New York Mets look like a team to monitor for the Japanese star.
articles.body:
With Teruaki Sato set to be arguably the most sought-after position player in free agency, the New York Mets look like a team to monitor for the Japanese star.

Per Chelsea Janes of SNY, president of baseball operations David Stearns went to Japan "as soon as the Mets' season ended" specifically to watch the Sato play for the Hanshin Tigers.

"You don't make that trip if you aren't seriously considering making a push for him," Janes wrote.

Hanshin announced on Oct. 19 that Sato would be posted for MLB teams this offseason. The 27-year-old is not subject to international free-agent rules, giving him a 45-day window to negotiate a deal without financial restrictions with all 30 MLB clubs after he is posted.

MLB.com's Mark Feinsand ranked Sato as the top position player and No. 4 overall free agent in the upcoming class, behind Tarik Skubal, Michael King and Freddy Peralta.

According to Feinsand, Sato has drawn comparisons to Munetaka Murakami thanks to his prodigious power and high strikeout totals. He has hit 79 homers and struck out 327 times in 1,211 plate appearances over the past two seasons in NPB.

Murakami came to MLB with big questions about his ability to make contact, which likely led to him signing a lower-than-expected deal with the Chicago White Sox for $34 million over two years.

The strikeout issues for Murakami weren't proven wrong with 196 in 553 plate appearances this season, but he also walked enough to post a .347 on-base percentage and slugged 35 homers to help the White Sox make a surprise playoff appearance.

Sato figures to benefit from Murakami's success, as well as being arguably the best power bat available in a soft free-agent class. Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki, Jake Bauers and Brandon Lowe are the other notable position players who can hit the market.

Stearns is already under an intense microscope from fans in Queens after the Mets missed the playoffs for the second consecutive seasons. Their 74-88 record this year was their worst in a 162-game season since 2017 (70-92).

After having the highest payroll in MLB in 2026, the Mets aren't going to get much contract relief unless they make some trades. Bo Bichette and Chris Devenski are their only potential free agents.

Bo Bichette could opt out of his deal worth $42 million in 2027, but his struggles this season would seem to make it unlikely he decides to test the market this offseason, particularly given the labor uncertainty with the current CBA set to expire on Dec. 1.

Mets owner Steve Cohen has not shied away from aggressively spending in the interest of improving the roster.

If Cohen believes Sato can be a difference-maker that gets them back to being competitive in the NL East, it wouldn't be a surprise if the five-time NPB All-Star signs with the Mets.
